summary.intent: Improve error observability for Claude CLI summary generation in PR #876: replace a silent 30s timeout with actionable typed errors, real-time streaming progress, and a TTY-gated deadline strategy so users understand why summary generation fails or hangs.
summary.outcome: Two stacked PRs were shipped: #963 (typed Claude CLI error classification — auth/rate-limit/config/cli-missing — with user-facing messages) and #964 (stream-driven progress display using --output-format stream-json, idle-based watchdog for non-TTY, 30min hard wall-clock cap, and legacy CLI fallback for older claude versions). Four rounds of multi-agent review caught and fixed bugs including ttft_ms field placement, idle watchdog misclassification, and incorrect timeout duration in error messages.

repo: Claude CLI operational errors (auth 401/403, rate-limit 429, config 4xx) return exit code 0 with `is_error: true` + `api_error_status` in stdout JSON — gating typed error extraction on non-zero exit misses all common failures

The summarization stack has three layers with distinct responsibilities: explain.go (policy/UX), summarize/claude.go (agent-agnostic), agent/claudecode/generate.go (subprocess); typed errors must stay unwrapped across summarize layer so explain.go can errors.As them

Auto-summarize is a completely separate code path (strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go::generateSummary) that calls summarize.GenerateFromTranscript directly with no timeout — a different problem from explain --generate

cmd/entire/cli/status_style.go already provides statusStyles (lipgloss), isTerminalWriter, shouldUseColor (honors NO_COLOR), and formatTokenCount — reuse these instead of introducing new lipgloss dependencies
IsAccessibleMode() in cli/utils.go provides screen-reader mode detection; must gate in-place \r updates on !IsAccessibleMode() for accessibility

charmbracelet/huh is forms-only (Select, Confirm, Input); lipgloss is the right tool for styled progress lines; bubbletea/bubbles want to own the render loop and conflict with line-based stderr output
Tests that modify package-level vars (defaultTextGeneratorFactory, summaryDeadlineResolver) cannot call t.Parallel() per CLAUDE.md — failure to follow this causes data races under go test -race
The claude CLI emits ttft_ms at the outer stream_event envelope level (sibling to 'type'), not inside the nested 'event' object — a fabricated test fixture can mask this struct field placement bug

code.finding: TTFTms must be on StreamEvent (outer envelope), not StreamInnerEvent (nested event object). Real CLI fixture confirms ttft_ms is a sibling of 'type':'stream_event', not inside 'event'. Fabricated test JSON masked this for multiple review rounds.

PhaseDone is emitted directly in GenerateTextStreaming (not via makeProgressDispatcher) because it requires final envelope data (OutputTokens, DurationMs). This split must be documented; otherwise future StreamingTextGenerator implementors won't know to emit PhaseDone themselves.

Idle watchdog cancels via context.WithCancel → context.Canceled, not DeadlineExceeded. Without checking the idleFired atomic.Bool first, idle timeouts were misclassified as user cancellations and showed the wrong message. idleFired must be checked before the Canceled sentinel.

Original code called settings.Load() three times per summary generation (summaryDeadlineResolver + settingsTimeoutUnset + error path). Replaced with summaryDeadlineResult struct returning deadlineMode enum (none/idle/hardClock) + duration in a single resolution.

GenerateFromTranscript originally mutated the caller-owned *ClaudeGenerator to backfill Progress field. Fixed by cloning the struct instead — the mutation would persist across calls if the caller reused the generator.

summaryProgressWriter.lastActivity must be seeded with time.Now().UnixNano() at construction. If initialized to 0, the idle watchdog's 'if ts > 0' guard prevents it from ever firing when no progress events arrive — the test hung for 10+ minutes before this was caught.
Malformed NDJSON lines are silently skipped. The malformedLines counter should be included in the 'stream ended without result' error message so CI users can diagnose corrupted output streams.

looksLikeUnrecognizedFlag must require BOTH a rejection phrase (unknown flag, unrecognized option) AND the name of a streaming-specific flag (stream-json, --include-partial-messages, --verbose) to avoid false-positives on legitimate API error messages.

workflow: Cherry-picking commits across diverged branches gets messy quickly; overlaying full file contents (git checkout <branch> -- <file>) is more reliable than cherry-pick when the bases have diverged
Amending vs new commit: review fixes should always be separate commits, not amended into the original — amending rewrites history and hides what was fixed post-review
Multi-agent review (code, errors, types, tests in parallel) consistently catches different bug classes; running 4 agents catches more than running 1 twice
Test fabrication can mask struct field placement bugs — using real captured CLI output as test fixtures (testdata/*.jsonl) prevents this class of false-green test

The simplifier skill (pre-commit) and the pr-review-toolkit (post-commit) serve different purposes and should both be run; the simplifier catches redundancy before review, the toolkit catches behavioral bugs during review
Codex adversarial review consistently surfaces architecture-level concerns (no hard cap, backward compat) that implementation-focused reviewers miss
PR splitting by natural seam (typed errors vs streaming/UX) is more effective than splitting by file count; each PR should deliver independent user value

friction: Idle watchdog lastActivity=0 bug caused test suite to hang for 10+ minutes before the root cause was identified — no timeout on test run meant a silent hang
ttft_ms struct placement bug survived multiple code review rounds because fabricated test JSON placed the field in the wrong location, making the wrong code appear correct
Cherry-pick approach for splitting the large PR into two stacked PRs got messy with conflicts; had to abandon and use full-file overlay instead
Accidentally amended a commit instead of creating a new one for review fixes, requiring a hard reset and re-applying changes
The wall-clock cap error message reported the idle timeout duration (5min) instead of the cap duration (30min) — discovered only in round 3 of review after the feature was already considered done
Multiple review rounds (4 total) were needed to converge on a clean implementation; each round found at least one real bug rather than just style issues
open_items: Auto-summarize hang protection: strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go::generateSummary has no timeout at all and runs at commit time — a parallel problem to explain --generate that was explicitly deferred
Codex adversarial finding: success envelope accepted even when cmd.Wait() returns non-zero exit — currently debatable (result is valid if fully written before teardown error) but not resolved
Per-summary cost display: the stream provides input/output token counts; surfacing these to users was noted as a trivially addable follow-up

looksLikeUnrecognizedFlag pattern list is narrow — if the legacy fallback fails to trigger on a real older CLI, users will get a streaming parse error instead of a graceful fallback; needs real-world validation against older claude CLI versions

The Generator interface has no progress capability; non-ClaudeGenerator implementations silently drop the progress callback — if new generators are added, either the interface needs extending or a ProgressAware interface should be introduced
